issues.failure_explanation: The energy error estimates of Theorem thm: wellposedness nonlin and Theorem thm: full model concentration rely on coercivity of the SIP form. By Lemma lemma: coercivity sip, coercivity holds only if the stabilization parameters satisfy sigma*eta > C_tr^2 (d+1) Dmax^2/Dmin (for the acoustic form D=1 with sigma=1 this reads eta > C_tr^2 (d+1)). Neither theorem imposes any condition on eta or sigma. For insufficiently large eta the SIP form is not coercive, the |.|_dG terms on the left-hand sides of the energy inequalities (e.g. eq: nonlin error first form) are lost, and the Gronwall argument producing the h^{2q} bounds breaks down.

failure_location.quote: Let the acoustic parameters satisfy $\csq$, $ \beta> 0$, and $\kappa \in \R$. Let the assumptions on $\triangles$ made in Section~\ref{sec: dG discretization} hold.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to Theorems thm: wellposedness nonlin and thm: full model concentration the standard assumption sigma*eta > C_tr^2 (d+1) Dmax^2/Dmin (with D=1, sigma=1 for the acoustic form). All statements, proofs, and rates then stand unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The hypotheses of both main theorems are incomplete: without a lower bound on the penalty parameter the claimed semi-discrete energy estimates, and hence the well-posedness and optimal-rate conclusions, are not guaranteed.
issues.title: Main theorems omit the SIP penalty-parameter condition needed for coercivity
issues.why_classification: The repair adds a standard local parameter condition; the method, conclusions, rates, and advertised scope all survive with no new argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\locainterpolant \phi$ is the local continuous interpolant, which satisfies the following standard estimates.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem prescribes discrete initial data (I_h p_0, I_h p_1) with I_h the nodal ('local continuous') interpolant, whose definition and whose cited stability/approximation properties require point values, i.e. a continuous function. p_0 in H^{q+1} is fine, but p_1 is assumed only in L^infty(Omega), and p in Xp yields merely p_1 in H^q(Omega) cap L^infty(Omega) (since p_t in H^1(0,T;H^q) subset C([0,T];H^q)). In the admitted regime d=2, q=1, H^1 cap L^infty functions may be discontinuous, so I_h p_1, the initial datum of the ODE system (eq: nonlin system of odes), and the identity e^{h,p}_t(0)=0 used in the error analysis are not defined there.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to p_1 in H^{q+1}(Omega) (then q+1 > d/2 in all covered cases, so p_1 is continuous and I_h p_1 is well defined); this is consistent with p_t in L^infty(0,T;H^{q+1}) and requires no other change.
issues.overall_effect: In the regime d=2, q=1 (explicitly allowed by the theorem), the semi-discrete acoustic solution is not constructed as stated, so the well-posedness and error results for the pressure, and through them Theorem thm: full model concentration, lack a valid object.
issues.title: Nodal interpolant I_h p_1 is not defined under the stated L^infty assumption on p_1
issues.why_classification: A slightly stronger, standard regularity assumption on p_1 closes the gap; the regime, method, and rates are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The discrete data are assumed only L^2 in time, and the accuracy assumptions (approx properties source terms) are L^2-based. The right-hand side F of the first-order system (eq: nonlin system of odes) is then merely L^2 in t, so p^h_tt = F cannot be continuous in general (e.g. take f_p^h discontinuous in time): no solution with p^h in C^2([0,T];V_h^q) need exist, and the classical Picard--Lindeloef theorem cited in prop:added-1, which requires continuity of F in t, does not apply as stated. The same overstatement affects u^h in C^1([0,T];V_h^q) in Theorem thm: full model concentration, and the scheme equations hold only a.e. in t rather than 'at all times t in [0,T]'.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for $\eps>0$ that will be fixed in the upcoming proof (see \eqref{def eps})

issues.failure_explanation: The bootstrap time t*_h in (eq: def thh) is defined for a parameter eps>0 that the proof promises to fix, and it is fixed as eps = (ell-1)/ell with ell = max{3d/(d+3),1}. For d=1, ell=1, so the chosen value is eps=0, violating the requirement eps>0 under which t*_h was defined. The remaining steps happen to close in 1D even with eps=0 (Lemma lem: unif bound pht needs only eps >= (ell-1)/ell, and the final comparison tnorm{p^h - I_h p} <= C h^q < C_0 h^{d/3+eps} needs only q >= 1 > 1/3 + eps), but as written the proof in the admitted case d=1 fixes a parameter value incompatible with its own definition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For d=1 choose any eps in (0, q - 1/3) (e.g. eps = 1/3), or relax the requirement in (eq: def thh) to eps >= 0 noting the 1D argument closes with eps=0; no estimate or rate changes.
issues.overall_effect: In the 1D case the definition of the bootstrap time t*_h is not matched by the parameter actually chosen, so the 1D proof of Theorem thm: wellposedness nonlin is not literally complete; Theorem thm: full model concentration inherits this through its reliance on Theorem thm: wellposedness nonlin.
issues.title: The chosen epsilon vanishes for d=1, contradicting the required epsilon>0 in the bootstrap definition
issues.why_classification: A degenerate-case parameter fix; every estimate, rate, and regime is preserved with no new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The energy estimate (prop: nonlin error bound) and the defect bound (lem: bound defect, via ||1+kappa p^h|| <= 1+r+r_0) require p^h(t) in the non-degeneracy set A_h for all t in [0,t*_h]. The only membership actually proved is at the single endpoint t*_h, and it is proved using Proposition prop: nonlin error bound itself, so the argument is circular unless membership on the whole interval is secured independently. It is not: (eq: def thh) imposes only the triple-norm condition at the final time, from which membership would follow only after an additional unstated smallness constraint on C_0 (the a priori bound gives |kappa| ||p^h||_L^infty <= C C_0 + r + o(1), since the boundary-face contribution scales like h^{eps-(ell-1)/ell} = h^0). A first-exit/continuity induction closes the argument with ingredients already present, but it is absent from the source.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard continuation argument: membership holds at t=0 (lem: p0 in D); on any interval where it holds, prop: nonlin error bound yields the O(h^q) error bound, which via (eq: wellposedness estimate2)-(eq: wellposedness estimate3) implies membership with strict margin; by continuity it then holds on all of [0,t*_h]. Alternatively include membership in the definition of t*_h. No new estimates are needed.
issues.overall_effect: The bootstrap proving Theorem thm: wellposedness nonlin contains an unverified link: the uniform energy and defect bounds are derived under a non-degeneracy property that is only checked at the final time by means of those same bounds.
issues.title: Non-degeneracy membership of p^h(t) on the whole bootstrap interval is used but never established
issues.why_classification: The gap is closed by a short, standard bootstrap-closure argument using only ingredients already in the paper; no claim, rate, or regime changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: split the error $u-\uh = u - \Ih u + \Ih u - \uh \eqqcolon \eI + \ehu$
The result then follows by applying \Gronwall's inequality.

issues.failure_explanation: The scheme (dG semi-discrete wave-adv diff system) allows arbitrary u_{0,h} in V_h, and Theorem thm: full model concentration imposes no condition on it, unlike the pressure initial data in Theorem thm: wellposedness nonlin. The proof's Gronwall step yields ||e^{h,u}(t)||^2 <= C h^{2q} + C int_0^t ||e^{h,u}||^2 only after discarding the initial term, which requires ||e^{h,u}(0)||_{L^2} = ||I_h u_0 - u_{0,h}||_{L^2} <= C h^q. As stated, the claimed estimate is false: with u_0 != 0 and u_{0,h}=0 one has ||u(0)-u^h(0)||_{L^2} = ||u_0||_{L^2}, which is not O(h^q) at t=0.

failure_location.quote: then there is a unique solution $(\ph,\uh) \in C^{2}([0,T];\Vhq) \times C^{1}([0,T];\Vhq)$ of \eqref{dG semi-discrete wave-adv diff system}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prescribe u_{0,h} = I_h u_0 (mirroring the pressure initial data), or assume ||u_{0,h} - I_h u_0||_{L^2} <= C h^q; the proof then goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The concentration error estimate of Theorem thm: full model concentration, and the overshoot bound in Section 'Bounds on the approximate concentration' that cites it, are unsupported as stated unless the discrete initial concentration approximates I_h u_0.
